items.followUp: Differentiate between organ level and organ-system level of biological organization.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the two levels by defining the cell as the basic unit and tissue as a group of similar cells.
rubric.description: Defines cell level and tissue level.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the cell as the basic structural and functional unit and a tissue as a group of similar cells.

rubric.why: States what the cells in a tissue have in common.
rubric.description: States that cells in a tissue perform a common function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the similar cells work together to perform the same function.

modelAnswer: At the cell level, the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
At the tissue level, a group of similar cells works together to perform the same function.

items.followUp: Briefly describe the organ-system level of biological organization.

rubric.why: Identifies the biosphere as the global level containing Earth's ecosystems.
rubric.description: Defines the biosphere as the part of Earth containing all ecosystems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the biosphere as the sum of all ecosystems on Earth.

rubric.why: Recognizes the regions of Earth where life exists.
rubric.description: Mentions the life-supporting regions of Earth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to life on land, in water, and in the atmosphere.

modelAnswer: The biosphere is the highest level of biological organization and includes all ecosystems on Earth.
It comprises the parts of land, water, and atmosphere where life exists.

items.followUp: How can a biologist present collected observations so that they are easier to interpret?

rubric.why: Names a standard way of arranging biological data.
rubric.description: States that data may be arranged in tables.

rubric.why: Names a visual way of presenting biological data for interpretation.
rubric.description: States that data may be presented in graphs or charts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning graphs or charts.

modelAnswer: In the biological method, collected data are arranged systematically in tables.
They may also be presented as graphs or charts to make patterns easier to interpret.

items.followUp: What is a hypothesis, and how is it tested in the biological method?

rubric.why: Captures the evidence-based nature of a scientific theory.
rubric.description: Defines a theory as a well-tested explanation supported by repeated investigations.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a theory is a well-tested explanation based on repeated evidence or experiments.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a law as a concise description of a regular pattern in nature.
rubric.description: Defines a law as a statement describing a consistent natural phenomenon.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a law describes a regular or consistent natural phenomenon.

modelAnswer: A theory is a well-tested explanation of natural phenomena, supported by repeated investigations and evidence.
A law is a statement that describes a consistent pattern or phenomenon in nature.

items.followUp: What does classification contribute to the study of biodiversity?

rubric.why: Identifies the central task of taxonomy.
rubric.description: Defines taxonomy as the science of naming and classifying organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that taxonomy deals with naming and classification.

rubric.why: Identifies systematics as the broader study of organismal diversity and relationships.
rubric.description: Defines systematics as the study of organismal diversity and relationships.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that systematics studies diversity and relationships among organisms.

modelAnswer: Taxonomy is the science of naming and classifying organisms.
Systematics is the study of the diversity of organisms and their relationships, including their evolutionary relationships.

items.followUp: Give two ways in which classification helps biologists study organisms.

rubric.why: Recognizes that grouping organisms makes their study manageable.
rubric.description: States that classification simplifies the study of organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that classification organizes organisms into groups and simplifies their study.

rubric.why: Identifies a practical purpose of classification.
rubric.description: States that classification helps identify organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning identification or showing relationships among organisms.

modelAnswer: Classification organizes the great variety of organisms into groups and makes them easier to study.
It helps identify organisms and understand relationships among them.

items.followUp: How did Robert Hooke's observation of cork contribute to cell biology?

rubric.why: Identifies the historical observation and material examined by Hooke.
rubric.description: States that Hooke examined cork in 1665.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning the year and cork.

rubric.why: Describes what Hooke saw and the name he gave the compartments.
rubric.description: States that Hooke saw small compartments and named them cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the compartments and their name.

modelAnswer: In 1665, Robert Hooke examined a thin slice of cork under a microscope.
He observed many small, box-like compartments and named them cells.

items.followUp: State two functions of the endoplasmic reticulum.

rubric.why: Identifies the processing role of the Golgi apparatus.
rubric.description: States that the Golgi apparatus modifies proteins and lipids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning modification or processing of proteins and lipids.

rubric.why: Identifies the sorting and transport role of the Golgi apparatus.
rubric.description: States that it packages materials into vesicles for transport or secretion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it packages or sorts materials into vesicles for transport or secretion.

modelAnswer: The Golgi apparatus modifies and sorts proteins and lipids received from the endoplasmic reticulum.
It packages them into vesicles for transport or secretion from the cell.
